messages:
marta: Heads up — saw a p99 latency spike for tenant acme-corp starting 2024-11-05 11:02 UTC. Customer reports autocomplete delays. Trace id: trace:abc123.

devon: Can you paste the top span timeline and the egress IP?

marta: Span summary pasted from collector:
```
edge-select          12ms
tls-handshake        232ms  <-- huge
proxy-forward        8ms
application          4ms
```
No explicit region tag on the tls span. Resolved egress IP is 3.5.7.9.

tracer-bot: Trace link: https://traces.redwood.local/trace/abc123 (auto-ingested). Shows TLS handshake waiting on remote.

ingrid: Any recent routing map or cert changes in prod region mapping?

ops-bot: Quick traceroute from edge node eu-west-1a to 3.5.7.9:
```
traceroute to 3.5.7.9 (3.5.7.9), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.9 ms
 2  52.21.11.1  1.2 ms
 3  * * *
 4  103.21.5.1  180.5 ms  <-- long jump to apac transit
 5  3.5.7.9  182.0 ms
```

devon: That jump looks like traffic landed on a fallback front in APAC. Could be SNI-based host routing mismatch. Do we have a client that strips SNI or rewrites host header?

marta: Repro curl from our staging worker using the egress IP:
```
curl -v --connect-to api.redwood.local:443:3.5.7.9 'https://api.redwood.local/v1/ping'
```
Response TLS cert CN: *.redwood-apac.internal and server_name reported: (none)

devon: Bingo. If SNI is missing or incorrect the front returns default vhost (APAC) which then routes into APAC backend. The extra network hop explains the 180-230ms delta.

ingrid: Why would SNI be missing? We didn't change SDKs. Any proxies between customer and us that might strip SNI?

marta: Customer uses an old corporate proxy appliance. Support note: "proxy rewrites TLS -> TLS inspection sometimes breaks SNI and replaces it with internal host".

devon: For immediate mitigation I can push a release that pins region selection using client IP geo as a stronger signal (avoid SNI path). Temporary routing policy snippet we’ll apply on the control plane:
```
route_policy {
  match: tenant_id == "acme-corp"
  prefer_region: us-west-2
  override_sni_routing: true
}
```
Applying as a short-lived rollbackable policy.

sre-oncall: I'll apply the policy to the affected tenant groups and watch p50/p95/p99 for 30m. Pushing now.

product: What's the customer impact window and how many customers affected?

marta: Affected: 3 enterprise tenants; acme-corp had ~2% of their requests go to APAC during the spike window (11:02–11:18 UTC). SE engaged.

devon: Longer term: we should add SNI validation alerts at edge and surface a flag when cert CN doesn't match expected env. Also consider fallback routing that keeps latency budget in the same cloud region rather than defaulting to nearest datacenter by config.

ingrid: Filing infra ticket to add SNI mismatch metric + circuit-breaker: INFRA-4321.

marta: I'll update the support ticket with repro steps and ETA for mitigation. Thanks all :thumbsup:

product: Keep me posted on customer reply and any billing credits request.

sre-oncall: Monitoring looks green so far; p99 back to baseline after policy. Closing follow-up in 1h unless regressions appear.
